title: Final Assembly — TUKU Pilot Independent Investigation 2026-06-13

Q1_F3_depth.question: Are the F3 depth claims in forensic documents (238-275 m, 79 m gap) contradicted by authoritative source files?
Q1_F3_depth.verdict: The well manager's classify table places F3 at 172.889-272.728 m, not 238-275 m. Driver well 09050331 screens 176-179 m, INSIDE the top 3.0 m of F3 (not 0 m overlap). The real instrumentation gap is 87.728 m of deep F3 below the 185 m well bottom. The mandate-hypothesis depth (172.889-272.728 m) is confirmed; the forensic 238-275 m / 79 m-gap framing is false.

Q2_kalman_vs_M8.question: Does the Kalman filter add value beyond the M8 level-reset at current visit cadence?
Q2_kalman_vs_M8.answer: NO at annual cadence (it IS the reset); MARGINALLY at monthly cadence + gap-aware uncertainty.
Q2_kalman_vs_M8.verdict: Annual Kalman gain = 0.997 (100% > 0.99) -> assimilation is a hard level-reset, no value-add over M8. Monthly gain = 0.9746 -> filter retains ~2.5% of the GPS-driven prediction, a small genuine blend. The ONE real advantage is gap-aware uncertainty: the Kalman band grows ~0.02268 mm/day between visits, vs the static conformal band that is fixed. For uncertainty quantification the Kalman interval is better; for the point estimate at annual cadence it equals the reset.

Q3_arx_verdict.question: Does ARX re-evaluation confirm, refute, or qualify the previous rejection?
Q3_arx_verdict.verdict: phi is NOT uniformly ~1 on grouped layers (range [0.4848, 0.9988]); only F3 (deep clay) is near-unit-root (phi~0.999). The 92.1% improvement is NOT reproducible vs a hold-last baseline (max 47.83%); the prior figure used a weak static-ratio baseline with no anchor. ARX adds modest real skill (18-48%) on F1/T1/F2/F3 but is worse than hold-last on T2/F4. Anchor-only does NOT cleanly match ARX (median repro 0.541). Net: the prior rejection was an artifact of the per-ring formulation; ARX is a modest, layer-specific contributor, not a column-wide winner, and remains below the carrier+GWL seq skill.

Q4_mcr_viable.question: Is MCR-AR a viable alternative to the carrier model for per-layer decomposition?
Q4_mcr_viable.verdict: The observed 6-layer matrix is 99.72% one mode (SV2/SV1=0.052); only 1 component clears the >0.1 threshold. MCR k=1 already reaches R2=0.99596; a 2nd component adds <0.3% variance. MCR can nominally place F2 and F3 under different components at k=2, but that lives in the 0.28% residual and is not a robust physical process. The 'six per-layer reconstructions are one GPS curve split by constants' degeneracy is real. MCR-AR is an in-sample curve fit, not a deployable per-layer decomposition superior to the carrier.

Q5_coverage_defensible.question: Are any of the coverage claims from the sequential rehearsal defensible?
Q5_coverage_defensible.answer: PARTIALLY — at band-defined visit dates yes; under all-dates sparse cadence no.
Q5_coverage_defensible.verdict: Every headline RMSE in metrics.json reproduces EXACTLY from its own innovation list (the prior 'not reproducible' claim is refuted). Coverage at band-defined visits is [0.667, 0.95] (median 0.875), below the 0.95 nominal but defensible as slightly under-covered. The '0-33.3%' hypothesis is a mischaracterization drawn from the sparse 'none'/'blackout' cells; it is true ONLY if coverage is demanded at every genuine date under annual/semiannual cadence (0.15-0.40), which is the honest limitation: between annual visits the conformal band cannot keep the drifting prediction covered.

Q6_part2_ready.question: Is the project ready for Part 2 (37 stations)? If not, what specific blockers remain?
blockers: DOC INTEGRITY: forensic F3 depth claims are false; correct provenance docs before scaling.
F2 annual skill <=0 vs anchor-once: at annual cadence the model adds no skill on the main aquifer; Part-2 stations on annual sampling will not beat a one-time anchor for F2.
T2 annual skill <=0 vs anchor-once (-0.092): aquitard prediction is not deployable at annual cadence.
Coverage 0.67-0.95 (<0.95 nominal) under realistic cadence; conformal bands need recalibration or gap-aware (Kalman-style) widening before per-station deployment.
Rank-1 degeneracy (99.7% one mode): per-layer separation is weakly identified at TUKU; spatial transfer to 8,577 grid points cannot rely on independent per-layer signals.
F3 deep instrumentation gap: ~87.7 m of F3 below the 185 m driver-well bottom is unmonitored; the depth-mismatched driver (screen 177 m vs clay to 272.7 m) is a physical limitation, not a code bug.
what_works: Monthly cadence skill is solid: F3 monthly skill_vs_anchor_once~0.558, F2~0.231 (honest table); coverage 0.78-0.95.
Carrier model is a reliable secular-trend tracker (carrier mean R2~0.94 in-sample); GPS captures the column trend.
metrics.json is internally consistent and reproducible — the reporting infrastructure is trustworthy.
F2 with the GWL head term reaches strong tail skill (carrier summary tail F2 skill +0.43).
Q6_part2_ready.recommendation: Deploy Part 2 ONLY for stations with monthly-or-denser MLCW sampling and a layer driver well screened within the target layer's compacting interval. Stations on annual sampling, or with deep layers lacking a depth-matched piezometer (the F3 situation), should be flagged as reconstruction-only with explicit uncertainty, not next-month prediction targets.
